summary.text: Mike Rounds is the Republican U.S. Senator from South Dakota, seeking a third term. A former insurance and real estate businessman, he served in the South Dakota Senate (1991-2000, including as majority leader) and as the state's governor (2003-2011) before his election to the Senate in 2014. He was re-elected in 2020 and won the 2026 Republican primary.

paragraphs.text: Born in Huron, South Dakota, in 1954, the eldest of 11 children; he has lived in the Pierre area since early childhood.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from South Dakota State University in 1977.
In the private sector he built an insurance and real estate business with offices across the state; Wikipedia identifies him as a former partner in Fischer Rounds & Associates.
Elected to the South Dakota Senate five times and served from 1991 to 2000, representing the Pierre area as minority whip (1993-1994) and majority leader (1995-2000).

Won the Republican nomination for governor in 2002 and was elected that November with 56.8% of the vote; he was re-elected in 2006 with 61.7%. He served as governor from 2003 to 2011 and chaired the Midwestern Governors Association in 2008.
Announced his Senate candidacy in November 2012 and won the 2014 Republican primary. He won the open seat in November 2014 with 50.4% of the vote and was sworn in on January 6, 2015.
Won re-election in 2020 with nearly 66% of the vote after defeating a Republican primary challenger, state Rep. Scyller Borglum, 75% to 25%.

According to his official biography, he serves on the Appropriations, Armed Services, Banking, Housing and Urban Affairs, Indian Affairs, and Select Intelligence committees. Wikipedia notes he co-chairs the Senate AI Caucus and was a member of the bipartisan Senate AI Working Group.

Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary with 75.8% of the vote over Justin McNeal, and received President Trump's endorsement in July 2025. He lives in Fort Pierre and has four children and 11 grandchildren, according to his official biography.
